statement: **Premise 0: analytic and ordinary calculus scope.** Analytic spaces have compact-neighbourhood bases; every ordinary open is an analytic domain with its canonical structure [CLD 11.1.7]. A topologically separated pure $n$-dimensional analytic space has the calibrated level-$n$ tropical structure, and analytic-domain calculus agrees with restriction [CLD 15.7.1--2]. A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically and differentially separated; compact supports admit smooth cutoffs, compact smooth localization, and uniform approximation of compact continuous scalars by smooth scalars [CLD 15.2.2--9]. This includes either valuation regime. Goodness and separatedness of the target and its ordinary opens give precisely this scope, without a global paracompactness assumption.
applicability: Original good separated pure boundaryless X and every ordinary open; no global paracompactness or valuation restriction.

statement: **Premise 1: generated Psh.** Psh is the smallest ordinary subsheaf of functions valued in $\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}$ containing smooth functions with positive smooth Hessian and closed under decreasing sequential limits [CLD Definition 8.1.1]. Its sheafified ordinal stages are: smooth generators at rank zero; ordinary-locally decreasing sequential limits of the previous stage at a successor; ordinary-local earlier-stage membership at a limit [CLD Lemma 8.1.4]. The assertion that this construction exhausts Psh, upper semicontinuity, and its cone operations are reconstructed below. The printed stabilization proof's unnecessary locally-integrable qualification is not used to change Definition 8.1.1.
applicability: No continuity imposed on predecessors; ordinal exhaustion, USC, bounded final selection and cone operations are freshly proved.

statement: **Premise 2: middle positivity and compact decomposition.** Every compact symmetric smooth $(q,q)$ test is a difference of two compact middle-positive smooth tests, when its support lies in a paracompact locally differentially separated open [CLD 6.5.2]. The theorem explicitly includes compact support on an almost-good analytic space, so good suffices here. Middle-positive currents are symmetric functionals nonnegative on middle-positive tests; positivity is ordinary-local [CLD 7.2.1--4]. A positive smooth factor wedged with a middle-positive current is middle-positive [CLD 7.2.7(b)]. No spanning assertion about strongly positive forms is used.
applicability: Compact tests on good, hence almost-good, ordinary analytic opens satisfy the theorem support scope. Middle cone is retained.

statement: **Premise 3: scalar coefficient measures.** On a locally differentially separated level-$n$ space, every positive scalar current is represented by a unique positive Radon measure [CLD 7.2.8]. For a middle-positive current $T$ and a smooth middle-positive complementary form $\eta$, its scalar coefficient measure $\mu_\eta$ satisfies $\int g\,d\mu_\eta=\langle T,g\eta\rangle$ for compact smooth scalars $g$, and is compactly supported if $\eta$ is compactly supported [CLD 7.2.11]. The source states locally bounded Borel multiplication in 7.2.12. We reconstruct its middle-positive order-zero justification rather than using the broader strongly-positive inference of 7.2.9.
applicability: Only positive coefficient measures and differences used; locally bounded Borel product continuity freshly proved.

statement: **Premise 4: topology and the middle cone.** In Euclidean coordinates a symmetric $(q,q)$ superform is middle-positive exactly when its signed coefficient matrix on the exterior power is positive semidefinite [CLD 1.2.6--7]. Positivity is tested on each tangent face. Test-form topology is the inductive topology of fixed compact supports and fixed moment presentations, with the cellwise coefficient seminorms; continuity may be tested after compact smooth localization to one chart [CLD 7.1.1--3]. The image of a compact analytic domain under a moment is a finite polyhedral set [CLD 12.2.4; the theorem cites its primary proofs rather than providing one]. Only this polyhedrality assertion is used, not the printed dimension-equality clause, which fails for a constant moment. This is the finite-face input for the coefficient bound below. None of these facts classifies a singular current.
applicability: Finite moment presentations of actual ordinary test families; middle matrix domination only. Only polyhedrality, not the printed dimension equality in 12.2.4, is used.

statement:
**Premise 5: restriction and differential identities.** Ordinary forms have compatible restriction, exterior products and Leibniz rules [CLD 3.3.10--12]. Ordinary currents form a sheaf; compact extension by zero defines restriction [CLD 7.1.6--7]. The current differentials obey

$$ (\mathrm d')^2=(\mathrm d'')^2=0,\qquad
\mathrm d''\mathrm d'=-\mathrm d'\mathrm d'',\qquad DJ=JD,\qquad
\langle DS,\alpha\rangle=\langle S,D\alpha\rangle $$

[CLD 7.7.1--5]. For smooth $s$ and a symmetric doubly closed $T$, $D(sT)=Ds\wedge T$ [CLD 8.5.3--4]. These identities concern the actual ordinary product on $W$.
applicability: Both closedness equations are imposed; identities are ordinary current identities on the original open.

statement: **Premise 6: canonical integration.** The boundaryless canonical integration current $\delta_X=[1]$ is positive and doubly closed [CLD 15.7.1, 7.7.4]. For a pure closed analytic subspace $Y$, $\delta_Y=\delta_{[Y]}$, with generic component multiplicities [CLD 16.6.3]. Thus applying our arguments to $\delta_X$ includes singularities and nilpotents with their original calibration.
applicability: Original calibration retained without nilreduction; actual generic lengths remain.

statement: **Premise 7: classical pluriharmonic geometry.** For any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation, [GR Definition 7.1] defines classical pluriharmonicity by requiring both signs to be classically psh. These functions are continuous and form a real vector space [GR 7.2]. On any affinoid $A$ with finite Shilov boundary $\Gamma$, a classical pluriharmonic function attains its maximum and minimum on $\Gamma$, and evaluation $\operatorname{PH}(A)\to\mathbb R^\Gamma$ is injective [GR 7.3, using the global maximum principle 6.4]. There is no good/strict/smooth/nontrivial-valued hypothesis in 7.3. We use this published analytic theorem only for functions already in $\operatorname{PH}(A)$, never to recognize a zero ordinary Hessian.
applicability: Only already classical pluriharmonic functions on fixed compact affinoid; GR allows trivial valuation and singular/nonreduced affinoids.

statement: **Premise 8: diagnostics, not recognition assumptions.** [GR 1.2] gives the inclusion of generated CLD Psh in classical psh, by functoriality, decreasing limits and the smooth-curve comparison. [GR 7.7--8] requires a nontrivially valued field and an **actual** strictly semistable formal model of a good quasicompact strict space to deduce real-PL regularity of already classically pluriharmonic functions. [GJR 10.17] instead starts with weak smoothness and a zero weak **form** Hessian, in its nontrivially valued good strict scope, and concludes harmonic real-PL regularity. [GJR 12.1--2] provides restriction of strong currents to ordinary tests, not a positive closed lift of every current and not product compatibility. These are used solely to audit the attempted routes; none supplies an assumption in Theorem 1 below.
applicability: Diagnostic scope only; no recognition, semistable model existence, arbitrary-current lift or compatibility assumed.
